summary: Renaming the heading to `## Do not flags` leaves the prefix lookup, entry count, and Defense assertions green although the required exact heading is gone.

The outer shell's TERM trap is deferred by POSIX until the foreground bash supervisor returns, so spawnSync's timeout: 900_000 kill (crew/seat-io.mjs:1727-1737) never terminates a hung gate — measured: a 4s timeout returned at 60s, the command's full duration, where the bare runner returned at 4.0s with signal SIGTERM.

The entire RV1-1 signal-forwarding fix is untested: deleting __crew_forward_signal and all three trap lines from a scratch copy leaves crew/drive.test.mjs at 310/310 and the acceptance gate at 16/0/0, so a later edit can silently reopen RV1-1; routing the forward through the injected $__crew_kill instead of the literal kill builtin is the cheap enabler for a deterministic test.

Carried forward unchanged: production still branches on `io.calls`, a test-fake-only property absent from the io contract (crew/io-contract.test.mjs:15-16), so an io that legitimately omits runClean skips the reap yet still tallies `unproven` and journals a gate_reap line for a measurement that never happened; the real fix needs crew/crew.test.mjs, outside files_in_scope.

Carried forward unchanged: 'the wrapped gate command sees the same shell contract as the bare runner' calls b127InvokeGate four times without a `dir`, leaking four mkdtemp directories per suite run while every other new test cleans up in a finally.

The finally sweep is unconditional over runner outcomes but not over driver liveness, so Ctrl-C on a foreground `crew run` (crew/crew.mjs:1393, no SIGINT handler) or the daemon's kill(-pgid) at crew/daemon.mjs:734-747 leaves the isolated gate group running with no sweep to reap it — measured: the gate's descendant survives a group SIGTERM (psExit=0) where the bare runner's is reaped (psExit=1); deferred because the failure brief forbids the trap mechanism by name and scopes half (1) to 'after the invocation returns'.

gateReapSweepCommand carries its own full copy of the probe/settle/kill ladder and only its happy path and idempotence guard are tested — the refusal arms, settle boundary and self-group guard are exercised for the wrapper and not at all for the sweep, and `grep -c sweep` over the acceptance gate is 0, so an edit missed in the sweep's copy is caught by nothing on the one path that runs when the wrapper was killed.

Carried forward with widened consequence: the `io.calls || typeof io.runClean === 'function'` predicate (a test-fake-only property, absent from crew/io-contract.test.mjs:15-16) now also gates the last-resort sweep, so an io that legitimately omits runClean gets neither wrapper nor sweep while still tallying `unproven` and journalling a gate_reap line; the triage told the builder to preserve it exactly and the real fix needs crew/crew.test.mjs, outside files_in_scope.

Carried forward unchanged: 'the wrapped gate command sees the same shell contract as the bare runner' calls b127InvokeGate four times without a `dir`, leaking four mkdtemp directories per suite run while every other test in the block cleans up in a finally.

The gate's own process group no longer receives signals sent to the driver's group, so Ctrl-C on a foreground `crew run` mid-gate (or the daemon's kill(-pgid) at crew/daemon.mjs:734-747) leaves the whole gate command running with the reaping shell dead — measured: gate child reaped before the change (ps exit 1), alive after it (stat S).

Out-of-plan branch `(io.calls || typeof io.runClean === 'function') ? wrapped : cmd` keys production behaviour on `calls`, a test-fake-only property absent from the io contract (crew/io-contract.test.mjs:15-16), so an io that legitimately omits runClean silently skips the reap yet still tallies `unproven` and journals a gate_reap line for a measurement that never happened.

'the wrapped gate command sees the same shell contract as the bare runner' calls b127InvokeGate four times without a `dir`, so four mkdtemp directories leak into /tmp on every suite run while every other new test cleans up in a finally.

A vacuous-green gate repaired into a genuinely-red gate that omits the GATE-SUMMARY line now escalates pre-build with zero builder rounds spent, even though the vacuous-green bounce brief — unlike the defective-red one at :2334 — never told the custodian to print that line and the green branch grants no second bounce.

Unchanged from round 1: the undeclared `trap ':' TERM INT` in the spawn wrapper is the only reason the exit marker exists in the SIGTERM path (measured), yet no plan section declares it and no test pins it, so removing it keeps the suite green while the documented top proof silently degrades.

Unchanged from round 1: reseat accepts `retired: true` as a free seat although retire no longer clears an unproven reservation, so a pi that outlives the 2s SIGTERM settle leaves the marker, the next ensureProcess adopts the old session at crew/headless-rpc.mjs:298-303, and the run keeps the old model while modifier_attempts records the swap as applied.
The `reservation-mismatch` and `no-kill-target` reasons are still produced by no test; both map to unproven, so a regression there cannot falsely claim clean.
The Object.keys mapping over an already-asserted-empty dumpTable is still vacuous; it reads as a column-shape assertion and pins nothing.

The plan-mandated EPERM-to-ALIVE test is missing and no test produces outcome 'failed' from teardown(); collapsing the probe-alive branch into UNKNOWN keeps the whole suite and the gate green while `ledger.mjs seat-teardowns` reports leaked: 0 over a window that is genuinely leaking.

An undeclared `trap ':' TERM INT` was added to the spawn wrapper; measured directly, it is the only reason the exit marker exists in the SIGTERM path, yet no test pins it and no plan section declares it, so deleting it degrades the documented top proof to signal-esrch or an intermittent zombie-driven 'failed' with every test still passing.

reseat still accepts `retired: true` as a free seat although retire no longer clears an unproven reservation, so a pi that outlives the 2s SIGTERM settle leaves the marker, the next ensureProcess adopts the old session at crew/headless-rpc.mjs:298-303, and the run keeps the old model while modifier_attempts records the swap as applied.
The `reservation-mismatch` and `no-kill-target` reasons are produced by no test, so a regression in either would go unnoticed; both map to unproven, so a regression cannot falsely claim clean.

The EAGAIN kill mock in acceptance test C2 never runs: the fixture writes no pgid file, so probeMap returns UNKNOWN at the readFileSync throw in crew/reclaim.mjs:968, making the test's stated mechanism different from the one actually exercised.
The Object.keys mapping over an already-asserted-empty dumpTable is vacuous; it reads as a column-shape assertion and pins nothing.

Deleting the new `transport === 'pane' &&` guard leaves the full 1705-test suite green, so a later revert would let a pi planner seat on headless-rpc claim subagents:true, satisfy requires:['subagents'] with no shortfall, and boot via rpcCommand's --no-extensions with no agent tool at all.

The pre-spawn arm feeds a 55KB agent name but asserts bounds only on content and details.refused, so making boundAgentName a no-op keeps all 23 arms green and b33's 52,287-byte details.agent regression (subagent.ts:471, :753) would land undetected.

Dropping the message.role !== 'assistant' filter survives the suite, so a regression would fold a nested tool's message_end into the child's spend and double-count the journal usage row and pi's own /session totals with no second source to catch it.

Interpolating the model-supplied agentName into the not-granted refusal keeps the suite green because the arm asserts byte bounds but never the absence of its own REQUEST_MARKER, so the payload-free property gate check G2 pins has no repo-side test.

The new entry claims [supersedes: 2026-08-01 — no lint or typecheck tooling exists] while its own Why reaffirms that entry and line 44 is left unmarked, so a reader hits a live, accurate entry that a newer entry claims to have replaced, against the file's own line-3 rule and its :43/:114 precedent.

The --checkout guard is fsExistsSync only, so `--checkout package.json` is accepted and the run reports a green exit-0 'would dispatch: nothing' instead of refusing missing-checkout, hiding a typo'd path as an empty board.
A valid optional lead unseat with cell:null is rejected by invented band and cost failures, so it cannot stage or compose.
A successful staged drop updates only staged and the diff, while the seats rail keeps rendering the original payload seat.
A degraded ladder still permits an optional cell:null move to stage and compose because null applicability is checked before ladder degradation.
A rejected later drop disables Compose for the unchanged prior valid staged set by overwriting stagedResult with the failed attempt.
A final target that is an existing regular file is swallowed as EEXIST, so openRun chmods state/ledger from 0644 to 0700 before degrading instead of failing without modifying it.
Replacing the helper body with recursive mkdirSync still passes the deep-path and nested-file test, so the procfs spin can return with repository CI green.
An active agent_sessions row with NULL billed fields is reported as no agent_sessions rows, falsely hiding its session count and diverging from the CLI.
A second run sharing a settled predecessor's task-return is forked, then falsely settled from that predecessor's envelope, allowing concurrent children on one checkout.
Enqueueing another run for a settled crew deletes the shared task-return envelope, making the first run lose its result and terminal state.

An operator following README:60 runs `--tier build --model-builder gpt-5.6-luna` and now gets band-unknown, because pi spells that ratified utility member `openai-codex/gpt-5.6-luna`; README:59-65 and :146 document the --tier passthrough and say nothing about provability, and README is outside files_in_scope so only a follow-up can fix it.

Mutating the ambiguity guard `matches.length === 1` to `>= 1` leaves crew/crew.test.mjs 161/161 green, so the design's safe direction (several matches is unknown) is unpinned — no collision is producible with today's seven members under adapter-pi or adapter-claude, hence a consider, but a colliding-stub fixture would pin it inside the file this lane owns.

Test 5 asserts only that the fenced and unfenced runs are equal to each other and never pins the expected outcome, so a mutation that breaks both branches identically (e.g. making the plan check unconditional) still passes it; killed only by its neighbours, not by itself.

A crew booted --fences/--lane and then run through the daemon reaches driveTask via child.mjs with no laneFence in ctx, so it is silently unfenced with no refusal and no journal row saying the fence was dropped — the plan's declared slice-2 gap, confirmed real; the remedy needs a file this lane's register does not grant.

The old paths' deletions are unstaged while the new paths are staged (git ls-files still holds blobs 21bd010/7acc168), so a default index-only `git commit` lands a commit carrying BOTH crew/realio.mjs and crew/seat-io.mjs — B1/A1 red on that commit and a duplicated io module shipped; `git add -A crew/` before committing fixes it.

Five pre-existing line-pinned citations into the renamed module are still wrong (ledger-queries.md:47,53; shape.mjs:7,9; trace.js:5,7 — e.g. crew/seat-io.mjs:312 is `return writes`), so a reader who sees C1/C2 derive two citations in this diff reads the rest as verified; plan-deferred per #327's file-it-and-leave-it rule, worth one follow-up issue.
A later promoted row has no synthetic premise, so it records NULL fields despite belonging to the already-checked original sweep.
Clean, unresolved, and unknown notes omit the mandated verdict prefixes, so persisted notes do not match the specified shapes.
A URL with userinfo is mis-extracted as a relative path (and @-named path segments are mangled), causing false premise failures instead of URL exclusion.
With no gate_cmd, review-exhaustion convergence calls gateRed:false and opens a PR claiming the acceptance gate is green even though no gate ran.

Plan test T8 is missing: replacing settleSeatTeardown(io) in crew/crew.mjs:1094 with an inlined copy of the old child.mjs block leaves the full suite unchanged (1238 pass both runs), so nothing in the repo stops the settle path being forked back into an entrypoint once task/gate.mjs C7 is gone.

The 'escalation -> NEVER teardown' lifecycle comment now sits below an unconditional settleSeatTeardown(io), so a reader concludes an escalated run leaves its rpc workers alive when it now SIGKILLs them; behaviour is fine (parkSeats records warm panes only and session_id survives), the comment is not.

Carried over from RV1-2 and still unchanged: the 'escalation -> NEVER teardown' lifecycle comment sits below an unconditional settleSeatTeardown(io), so a reader concludes an escalated run leaves its rpc workers alive when it now kills them; behaviour is correct (parkOnOutcome runs earlier, parkSeats records warm panes only, session_id survives), the comment is not.

Plan tests 21/22 absent: swapping the survivor/checkProofNote precedence leaves both npm test and the acceptance gate green, so a run with a PROVEN gate survivor plus a later io throw records non-blocking 'unproven', never spends the gate repair, and commits behind a gate that does not discriminate.

Plan test 7's errored/no-summary survivor variants absent: deleting `baselineGateDefect(res.output) ||` from the why chain leaves suite and gate green, so a mutated run that CRASHES a check while printing `FAIL <check>` (the test file's own THREW fixture shape) is recorded outcome:'killed' and check_discrimination:'proven'.

All 14 rejection cases assert `errors.every(e => e.why)`, which is true for an empty array, so the test asserts nothing; measured, widening CHECK_LABEL (drive.mjs:865) to /^.+$/ keeps drive.test.mjs green and admits a space-bearing label that collides with the `FAIL <check>` matcher.

Plan test 24's two pre-build briefs are untested: dropping the stable-identifier note from gate-vacuous-bounce.md or gate-defect-bounce.md individually keeps the suite green, so a planner repairing a vacuously-green gate can rename checks and manufacture a generation-2 survivor with the sole gate repair already spent.

Plan test 10's missing-file case is absent, so the `original === null` unapplied branch never executes under suite or gate; a regression there sends the planner — on its one repair — to fix a find string when the file itself is missing.

Measured by driving driveTask with a readFile that throws new Error(''): check_discrimination reads 'proven' with checks:[] and the commit is taken — a pass that ran zero mutations claims proof; `throw null` instead raises a TypeError that escapes driveTask with no escalation envelope.

Plan test 25's stated requirement that the no-declaration gate-discrimination-bounce.md stay byte-identical is false: measured 943 bytes at HEAD vs 945 now, because the two new array entries evaluate to '' and each contributes a blank line through join('\n').

The FAIL <check> convention and label grammar reach the planner only through a replacement-gate bounce, so a first declaration is authored blind and a gate printing another failure format yields all survivors on first green, spending the sole gate_repairs on teaching an output format.

The test named 'stays byte-stable when no mutations are declared' asserts only that the two markers are absent, so reverting the guard at drive.mjs:2075 to the round-1 template form reintroduces a blank line in the planner brief while the test and the gate stay green; the behaviour itself is correct (measured byte-identical to HEAD).

Carried forward: the FAIL <check> convention and label grammar reach the planner only through a replacement-gate bounce, so a first declaration is authored blind and a gate printing another failure format yields all survivors on first green, spending the sole gate_repairs on teaching an output format; the planner-brief text is outside this lane's files_in_scope.
With config.readyColumn empty and a non-null dbPath, intakeRun unconditionally observes dispatches and creates/opens the ledger after intakeSweep's pre-I/O refusal.
The run header implies paired --lane/--fences support, so an operator can follow the prose and hit the new exit-2 refusal.

The new claim that `--agent-planner pi` boots with no shortfall waiver is unqualified, but adapter-pi.mjs:85 delivers subagents only on transport 'pane' — an operator adding --headless-all (or --transport-planner headless-rpc) on that promise gets a boot refusal because the planner charter requires subagents and the grant cannot flip it on rpc.

Grouping 025 with the retired runtime is true of its machinery (handover-spec.md, orchestration.md, agents/, role-boundaries.test.mjs all absent) but its decision — test ownership read off files_in_scope, not a spec field — is live in crew/drive.mjs:1663-1673 and docs/conventions.md:113, so a lane could read the note as retiring a convention the scope gate still enforces.

The crossing enumeration is import-only: crew/memory.mjs:11-13 also crosses into scripts/factory/ by subprocess (node scripts/factory/ledger.mjs task|sessions|run-set), which neither the bullet nor the gate's R1 import regex sees, so a reader counting crossings gets three files where four is honest.

Both amendment records and all seven markers are dated 2026-08-21 while the change lands on 2026-08-22 — the quoted ledger measurement really was taken on 08-21, so the record is a day behind its own commit rather than false, and the dates are gate literals (K1-K7, S1-S7) so changing them would be a gate repair, not a build fix.
A nonce-bearing reason is redacted after the unknown guard, so replaying that JSONL row throws for a missing reason.

settle's comment still claims "ONE settlement path for both exits" and teardown ordering "on the signal path exactly as on the return path", but there is no signal path and settle now has one call site (:300), so the `if (settled) return result` guard is unreachable — a future reader treats that guard as load-bearing for the very shape the new conventions entry exists to forbid, and restores it.

SIGNAL_KILL_BOUND_MS (1000ms, :1494) is compared against an `elapsed` measured entirely in the PARENT (:1527 to :1531), so parent event-loop starvation under npm test's parallel file execution can red a correct tree; the plan's "500x the measured 1-2ms" defense bounds child slowness, not that — margin is nonetheless ~20x against the whole 35-57ms test, measured over three runs.

The comment cites crew/child.mjs:138-141 for "the same escalation envelope a signalled child writes for itself"; that factory is now deleted outright, so the pointer dangles and no child writes that envelope — unfixable in this slice because crew/daemon.mjs is fenced to sibling lane b115-settlepaths, so it belongs to that lane or its own issue.
A complete startPhase mirror with seq 1e20 is tagged INTEGER on the JSONL side but stored REAL by SQLite, producing false drift_total 1.
A complete startPhase mirror at JS number -2^63 is tagged INTEGER in JSONL but stored REAL by SQLite, producing false drift_total 1.

The charter test omits the plan-prescribed doesNotMatch for 'consulted ONLY' / 'your ONLY loop', so restoring either claim to crew/roles/lead.md leaves the lead with two mutually exclusive return contracts and npm test still green — only the ephemeral task-dir gate.mjs:308 rejects them.

The lead-less failed-proof test matches the diagnosis with /acceptance gate|discriminat/i, which the guard's own boilerplate ('the acceptance gate needs a repair this crew cannot make') already satisfies — verified true against a message built with an empty diagnosis — so dropping proofNote() at crew/drive.mjs:2097 would ship a reasonless mechanical-tier escalation with the suite green.

The reviewer charter still tells the seat that issues the gate-defect verdict that 'gate' grants the planner its one repair (as does docs/adr/adr-030:141); both are outside files_in_scope, so this is deferred follow-up rather than a fix for this build.

A local-pi pi seat on headless-rpc can pass boot but starts without checkout config/grants, so ambient pi configuration can silently replace the declared endpoint; defer RPC plumbing or a transport-specific refusal.

Out-of-plan line `// Measured seconds: 1459 / 1800.` restates digits the prescribed sentence already carries, and is what kept the gate green under its own declared W10 mutation, costing the crew its one gate repair.

The argv read is a hand-written five-role literal beside a derived role set, so adding a role to WAITS_S yields a flag assertUsage accepts but runCmd never reads — the operator's value is silently dropped instead of refused; the fix would delete mutation W9's declared anchor, so it cannot land in this slice.

Acceptance criterion 1 is pinned only by the task-scoped gate — I measured that mutating `...WAIT_FLAGS,` to `...[],` leaves the whole repo suite green, so after close-out the wait flags can be dropped from KNOWN_FLAGS.run with no test failing.

The plan-prescribed insertion point leaves `# per-run round budgets` trailing the wait-flag lines, so an operator skimming usage sees two stacked explainers and must match the second back to flags three lines above it.

driveDirectedRound's summary carries ctx.briefFile and no commit_subject, so every directed run commits the subject "crew(<task>): directed by the task brief at <absolute machine-local path>" into permanent git history and demotes the builder's commit_message to the body; verified by calling composeCommitMessage with the exact envelope the round returns.

The conditional details.variant spread is a production edit absent from the plan's Changes list (gate check B1 requires it): details.variant exists for directed but not full/repair so nothing can rely on it, and the literal `variant === DIRECTED_STAGE_HEAD` now appears twice so the declared B1 mutation replaceAll-perturbs two sites instead of the one anchored.

The new array-seats refusal branch in shapeDefect is untested — replacing its condition with `if (false)` leaves drive/crew/daemon tests at 569 pass / 0 fail — so the guard that would refuse the next array-seat partial shape with mismatched required_seats is unproven (the shipped declaration itself is still pinned by the snapshot test).

Criterion 4's 'failing first tree read' is covered by no test: deleting crew/driver.mjs:288 (if (first.err) return unknown(...)) keeps all 22 tests green, and in that mutant first.ref is undefined so a top surface with no ref key is returned as a measured forest for the requested id.

The mandated literal p.pid === p.pgid is written as process.pid === process.pgid (normalize's parameter is named process), so the preserved C3 mutation's find-and-replace matches nothing and reports green without ever mutating the predicate; the same rename also shadows the global process used at crew/driver.mjs:11.
The provenance header drops the plan's explicit enumeration of retained fields, leaving 'pruned mechanically to the fields the helper reads' unfalsifiable by a reader of the inlined capture.

assertCompleteUnknown only checks reason is a non-empty string, so deleting crew/driver.mjs:288 keeps the suite green while a failing first tree read reports 'moved between snapshots: undefined then surface:27' instead of 'tree (before) failed: exit 1' — a journal diagnostic naming the wrong cause.
With NO_COLOR on Node 24+, injected '# fail 0' is the gate's first match, so a later real nonzero failure summary still passes C1.
With only DEVTEAM_BUDGET_MAX_TOKENS set, the required default window references an unimported RUN_SET_WINDOW_MS and GET /api/run-set returns 500.
An absent cell_failures readout with roster seats produces undetermined rows, but the absent branch hides every card so the required evidence is never rendered.
A failed root snapshot is incorrectly recorded as root-unidentified instead of unproven.
An unknown or permission post-SIGTERM probe can trigger SIGKILL and falsely produce a proven reclaim.
A final EPERM group probe is counted live/failed rather than probe-unknown/unproven.
The out-of-plan global process.kill shim can forge ESRCH for a group with an unsignalable foreign-uid member.
An EPERM/unknown root group probe marks a snapshot-bound live root dead and can then authorize signals to its descendant groups.
An EINVAL/unknown post-SIGKILL probe is counted as live/failed instead of probe_unknown/unproven.
Only nine committed tests exist, leaving the plan-required fresh-snapshot, signal-race, root, run-entrypoint, and ledger retry regressions unprotected.
An unknown final root-group probe after SIGKILL is recorded as failed/alive instead of unproven.
The out-of-plan zombie workaround temporarily replaces global process.kill and can forge ESRCH for synchronous callback probes.

The regex-escape character class is malformed so the replace is a no-op (verified empirically); the assertion builds a RegExp from the raw path, so a TMPDIR containing a metacharacter (e.g. /var/folders/q+/) makes this test fail red even though the brief holds the exact path, and an unbalanced [ makes new RegExp throw.

formatCountBasis's `used` branch is now unreachable for its only caller — baseline is commit_scoped, so profileField('baseline') can only return used:false with `recorded` — leaving dead wording that reads as live coverage to the next editor.

The `protected paths in force: N · <basis>` line carries only the profile basis, so a brief compiled with --protected as well counts those entries in N but names no file, leaving a reader unable to tell where the extra paths came from.
Literal protected-file prefixes misclassify legal paths such as crew/drive.mjs.bak, causing a pane run to escalate before any build despite no protected path in scope.
C13 trims porcelain status prefixes before slicing them, so valid in-scope crew paths become rew/... and the required gate exits 1.
An existing emitter sidecar can redirect daemon child usage to an old DB, leaving the configured budget ledger blind.
The Node 20 CI lane fails the new SQLite tests (including :1028) because node:sqlite is unavailable below the ledger floor.
A giant but accepted integer window_ms throws a raw RangeError at enqueue instead of producing a readable budget outcome.
On Node 20, a fresh configured ledger stays absent after JSONL-only emitter degradation, so every budget admission is incorrectly measured as zero.
A stale sidecar mismatch escalates and suppresses driveTask even when the daemon has no budget, making optional instrumentation load-bearing.
Node 22 can require node:sqlite but is below the emitter's Node 24 floor, so fresh budgeted work writes no DB while usageWindow repeatedly admits it as zero.
A launched ast-grep binary that exits nonzero is staged/logged as a successful proposal or apply, so a failed rewrite can be falsely reported as complete.

The comment still cites the builder's deny as "Task,Agent", so a maintainer grepping that string lands on it and concludes the builder is not denied Workflow; the file is outside files_in_scope, so the fix is deferred work.

The FANOUT_TOOLS paragraph is appended with no blank line to the 27-line SEAT_DEFAULTS block comment, so a reader going top-down reads the declaration's docstring as a continuation of the seat docs rather than as the doc for the one edit point this change exists to create.

A crew booted before this lands keeps deny: 'Task,Agent' in its crew.json and crew/headless.mjs:235 rebuilds --disallowedTools from that stored value, so an already-live builder can still fan out until re-boot; the defense (crew.json is written fresh at boot, crews are per-task) holds, so this is recorded, not work.

Acceptance criterion 13 demands git diff --numstat 21/11 for the ADR, but the plan's own byte-identical reference measures 20/10, so criteria 13 and 14 cannot both hold — the lead could bounce a correct build on it.

Deferred work the plan itself flagged: ADR-030's citations outside section 10 stay falsified — crew/drive.mjs:595-603, cited as the gate-reverify path, now resolves to re-ask id-rejection code, so a reader auditing Decision 2 lands on unrelated code.
A duplicate tier request overwrites the active crew's crew.json before the later run-active refusal.
Raw task equality misses slug aliases, allowing a duplicate tier boot to overwrite an active crew before run-active is raised.

The scout brief is joined with a literal backslash-n instead of a newline, so a real scout run hands the planner seat a single run-on line in which the heading, the no-write prohibition and the itemised envelope contract are fused together; drive.test.mjs:3489 and gate C12 only do substring includes(), so the mangling is invisible to the suite.

The drift tripwire's first loop asserts its own guard condition and can never fail, so removing a variant from VARIANTS while leaving its stale key in VARIANT_STAGE_PHASES keeps the test green and leaves realio mapping a stage head no shape can emit.

VARIANT_STAGE_PHASES[head] is an unguarded property read, so phaseForStage('toString:r1') returns a function that would flow into emitter.phaseTransition — unreachable today only because stage() now refuses undeclared heads; hasOwnProperty guards it in one line, the convention ledger.mjs:171 already uses.
An injected opener defaults existsSync to true, so a fresh nonexistent DB is opened/created instead of using the required closed no-open path.
The unplanned environment snapshot can apply stale breaker configuration while bootCmd awaits adapter resolution.
An injected opener forces existsSync true, so a nonexistent ledger with failed fake rows wrongly rejects instead of taking the required fresh-install closed path.
A date-unrepresentable but Number.isInteger window reaches toISOString and throws raw RangeError without naming CREW_BREAKER_WINDOW_MS.
The unplanned environment snapshot can apply stale breaker configuration if an embedding changes env while bootCmd awaits adapter resolution.

ENVELOPE_REFUSAL_REASONS is frozen but nothing enforces membership at the refuse() site, so a later refusal branch minting an off-set reason ships [field-order] into escalation.why unnoticed and the frozen export stops being the set of reasons that occur.
A board-fetch failure defaults considered to 0 and renders the false claim that the Ready column held nothing to refuse.
An omitted gate_path is undefined, so JSON journal serialization drops gate_path_rejected and loses the required rejection evidence.
A bare --memory-budget-bytes flag becomes true and Number(true) yields a one-byte budget rather than the required invalid-budget fallback.
When a valid tiny budget leaves no rendered section, the journal skips all over-budget drops and falsely records dropped: 0.
The unknown flag --__proto__ is lost through the plain-object setter, so stats succeeds at exit 0 instead of refusing it.
A prototype-named unknown verb with a flag calls accepted.has on an inherited non-Set, leaks a TypeError stack, and exits 1 rather than 2.
A preflight-failed crew subprocess leaves the prior returns/task.json in place, and dispatchRepair records that stale status:done envelope as a successful repair instead of unreadable.
If the started-record append fails after the continuation forks, the untracked detached child can later overwrite restored task.json despite terminal fallback settlement.
A prior child exit/error callback can orphan the newly forked continuation when poll observes the eligible envelope before the old child exits.
A regrant registry append failure after unlinking task.json loses the terminal envelope, leaving the fallback settlement unreadable as pending.
A failed continuation fork is returned by pump rather than thrown, so regrant reports success after deleting task.json and leaves the task orphaned without a terminal result.
A SIGCONT/SIGSTOP mutant passes because every nonzero signal is treated as death, while a live continuation could later overwrite the restored escalation.
With --model-reviewer openai-codex/gpt-5.6-luna, the actual boot seat is raw/null while shadow.seated falsely reports the displaced openai/gpt-5.6-terra roster cell.
A post-crash append joins a torn no-LF tail, losing that valid arm and making a later append refuse the whole manifest.
A minimally truncated tail such as `{` becomes an interior manifest-unreadable line after a later successful append, so collection still fails.
Two malformed adjudications for different findings in one dispatch both emit only 'dispatch d1', so the operator cannot identify which finding/ref each incomplete entry concerns.
